claim: Sequential focused training on new material overwrites old knowledge in a shared-weight learner; interleaving old with new prevents it (penguin net, AB-AC lists).
agent_test: Add a new lesson to the memory/skill store; compare re-solving old problems with the new lesson alone vs new lesson plus interleaved old problems. All simulations are from McClelland 1995 (one source); McCloskey and Cohen 1989 not opened.

claim: Consolidation in animals is graded: hippocampal lesions hurt recent memories more than old ones, with fitted decay from about 1 day (Winocur) to years (Squire and Cohen); Table 1 Dh per day 0.250, 0.050, 0.035, 0.001.
agent_test: Not directly testable in a scaffold; use as design prior: new lessons stay provisional for N problems before they may overwrite a rule. Primary studies read only through the 1995 paper. GAP SEARCH: Primary studies now opened (Anagnostaras 1999, Wiltgen 2006, Squire 2015 review). Gradient is real but measured at only 1 vs 50 days in the within-subject study; several labs find flat gradients (Lehmann 2007, Sutherland 2008, Sparks 2011, Broadbent and Clark 2013). The per-day decay rates in Table 1 are model fits, not measured curves, so treat them as a design prior only.

claim: In class-incremental settings, regularisation (EWC, SI) fails (about 20% on Split MNIST) while replay works (DGR 90.79, iCaRL 94.57, offline 97.94).
agent_test: Equal-token test: lesson store with do-not-touch flags vs replay of stored old problems; measure old-problem accuracy after 50 new lessons.
audit_note: Numbers match van de Ven Table (DGR 90.79, iCaRL 94.57, offline 97.94, EWC 20.01, SI 19.99); all numbers from one paper, DER supports regularisation failing in class-IL.

claim: Plain experience replay with a small buffer is a strong baseline; a tiny episodic memory (1 example per class) gives 7-17% gains and ER beats many specialised methods.
agent_test: Keep 1-5 exemplars per lesson as regression tests; compare against no regression set at equal tokens. GAP SEARCH: Independent evaluation (Soutif-Cormerais 2023) and Buzzega 2020 (+51.2 CIFAR-10 and +26.9 CIFAR-100 points from tuning ER) agree that tuned plain ER is very competitive.
audit_note: Chaudhry abstract gives 7-17% gain with one example per class; DER paper shows ER beating regularisation/other baselines; DER abstract itself is about logit-distillation variant.

claim: Output matching on replayed items (distilling the past model) adds a little over plain ER (MNIST-360 buffer 200: ER 49.27, DER 55.22, DER++ 54.16; at buffer 1000 the gap shrinks to 0.8).
agent_test: Store past answer plus reasoning with each regression item and check agreement, not only correctness.

claim: Explicit fast/slow dual-memory networks beat single-store replay in the authors' own tests (CLS-ER MNIST-360 buffer 200: 66.37 vs DER++ 54.16; FearNet mean 0.923 vs iCaRL 0.782).
agent_test: Two-tier agent memory (fast raw episodes, slow distilled rules) vs one tier. Kemker 2018 benchmark (b11) found all five mechanisms fail somewhere. Promising, not proven; all gains are self-reported by method authors. GAP SEARCH: Still no independent reproduction of CLS-ER, FearNet or DualNet: Soutif-Cormerais 2023 did not include them and found no clear winner among the methods it tested. Stays single-source.

claim: Pseudo-replay (generative) is weaker than real replay for LLMs: LAMOL diverged from upper bound where 1% real rehearsal reached 98.0-99.8%; 24,000 pseudo samples did not fix task-alignment loss.
agent_test: Compare regression set from real stored problems vs model-generated imagined problems. Contested because Shin 2017 and van de Ven show generative replay works on MNIST (DGR 90.79). GAP SEARCH: Zheng 2025: fewer than 20% of 24,000 LAMOL pseudo samples were valid after filtering. Agent-level real-vs-generated regression sets remain untested.

claim: In instruction-tuned LLMs, 0% rehearsal catastrophically forgets; 0.25% gives almost perfect stability; 1% rehearsal gives 98.0-99.8% of upper bound over 8 tasks.
agent_test: All lines are the one Scialom 2022 paper (T0). Test a replay-fraction sweep on our agent's lesson-update step.

claim: In continual pre-training, 1% replay cuts forgetting; 5% (weak shift) or 25% (strong shift) replay plus LR re-warming/re-decaying matches full retraining at 405M and 10B.
agent_test: Weight-level; not applicable to a prompt scaffold. a21, b14, c04 are the same paper (c04 lists author order wrongly as Gupta first).

claim: Forgetting after fine-tuning is partly lost task alignment rather than lost knowledge ('spurious forgetting'): old-task accuracy fell from near 100% to about 10% within 150 steps and is partly recoverable.
agent_test: When a new lesson degrades old performance, test whether re-cueing restores it before concluding the lesson conflicts. Two papers differ in mechanism (task inference skew vs alignment loss). GAP SEARCH: Zheng shows recovery by fine-tuning on half the old data or ten irrelevant instances (near 100% recovered vs about 10% raw accuracy); Kotha shows prompt-only recovery by translating the prompt (Alpaca drop 1.0% Leetspeak vs 56.75% English). Prompt-level re-cueing is plausible but untested for agent lessons.

claim: Scale does not clearly protect from forgetting: forgetting rose from 1.1b to 7.1b in BLOOMZ continual instruction tuning, while replay plus LR schedule matched retraining at 405M and 10B.
agent_test: a19, b12, c05 are one paper (Luo); different methods (instruction tuning vs pretraining). Not decision-relevant for a frozen-weights agent.

claim: LoRA learns less and forgets less than full fine-tuning; sparse memory finetuning cut NaturalQuestions F1 drop to 11% vs 89% full and 71% LoRA at equal new learning.
agent_test: Weight-update methods; our agent is frozen. Sparse result is one preprint (abstract re-confirmed this session). LoRA result rests on one paper (a22, b15 same).

claim: Gradient-trained models fail to use latent information (reversal curse: finetuning near zero, in-context near ceiling); in-context or retrieval memory generalises better, but only if training included sequences teaching context use (oracle retrieval about 12% and 6% without).
agent_test: Test: old lessons in context vs distilled into a summary rule, scored on reversed or derived questions at equal tokens. Two related Lampinen papers, same group (McClelland coauthor), so partly non-independent. GAP SEARCH: Lampinen 2025 shows fine-tuning on in-context reasoning traces closes much of the gap; the 12% and 6% oracle-retrieval numbers were not found in that paper and belong to c02. What practice teaches context use for retrieval stays open.
audit_note: 12% and 6% oracle-retrieval figures verified in Fig 7 caption of Lampinen 2025 latent learning; near-zero/near-ceiling reversal result verified in the second Lampinen paper (same lab, so effectively one group).

claim: Episodic retrieval stores (HippoRAG, HippoRAG 2, Larimar) improve multi-hop QA or editing: HippoRAG up to 20% over RAG and 10-30x cheaper than IRCoT; HippoRAG 2 +7% associative memory; Larimar edits 4-10x faster.
agent_test: HippoRAG draws on hippocampal indexing, not CLS replay. Same lab wrote HippoRAG 1 and 2. Lab-reported only.

claim: Weight-free fast learners work in agents: verbal reflection memory (Reflexion: +22% AlfWorld, 91% HumanEval pass@1) and reflection synthesis (Generative Agents: ablating reflection lowers believability).
agent_test: Only loosely CLS. Nobody tested interleaved re-checking of old items in agents. Run reflection memory with and without a replay-check against old tasks.

claim: Offline sleep-time compute on stored context cuts test-time compute about 5x at equal accuracy and adds up to +13% (GSM-Symbolic) and +18% (AIME); 2.5x lower per-query cost over 10 queries.
agent_test: Re-verified in abstract and body this session. Gain depends on query predictability. Test an offline consolidation pass of the lesson store between tasks, tokens counted. GAP SEARCH: Boundary: on the SWE-Features agent case study the gain was about 1.5x fewer test-time tokens at low budgets, and plain test-time compute was better at high budgets. Predictability of the query drives the effect. Still one paper.

claim: Updated CLS theory (2016): hippocampus replays salient or rare events preferentially, and schema-consistent information can be integrated into cortex fast (Tse 2007: 48 h, one-trial pairs).
agent_test: Contradicts the strict 1995 claim that integration must be slow and interleaved. Lessons that fit an existing schema may be safe to write directly; novel ones need replay. Tse primary papers not opened. GAP SEARCH: Agent-level support for gating consolidation (Zhang 2026: Retain/Delete/Consolidate doubled accuracy over forced consolidation) and for locking verified rules (Tablan 2026), but no study tests a schema-consistency gate itself. Animal side: Tse 2007 is cited by Squire 2015 (lesions at 3 h impaired, at 2 days spared); primary Tse paper still not opened.

claim: CLS ideas in AI are mostly realised as generative replay of past inputs; few models have hippocampus-to-cortex feedback in both directions.
agent_test: Review claim (Hayes 2021) plus conceptual mapping in Kumaran 2016.

claim: Replay share is not very sensitive in deep RL: 50-50 new/replay works, 75-25 and 100% replay also work; behavioural cloning on replay is needed.
agent_test: One paper (Rolnick CLEAR). Test replay share of 10/30/50% of regression budget.

claim: In frozen-weights LLM agents, forgetting reappears at the memory level: old and new experiences compete for the context window. Fine-grained per-step memory gave +15.0% forward transfer but -10.0% backward transfer in BabyAI; abstract insights gave +3.5 BWT vs raw -4.0.
agent_test: Track backward transfer (old-task accuracy after new lessons) for every lesson batch. Hu 2026 conflicts with Zhang 2026 on whether abstraction is safer; test both stores.

claim: LLM rewriting of lessons (consolidation) regresses problems already solved: GPT-5.4 went from 100% to 54% on a 19-problem ARC slice; mean accuracy on 33 tasks fell 58.5 to 38.5 by epoch 10; a raw-episode control stayed competitive. In tau-bench banking, distilled rules held banked solutions at 0.65 vs 0.88 for stored experience.
agent_test: Run a regression set of old solved problems after every lesson write; compare consolidate-always vs retain-raw-and-gate at equal tokens. Both sources are 2026 preprints on different tasks (ARC, tau-bench); no replay arm yet.
audit_note: All numbers verified in full texts (100->54 on 19-problem slice, 58.5->38.5, hold rate 0.88 vs 0.65, Mistral Large).

claim: Nobody has tested interleaved replay of old problems at lesson-write time in a frozen-weights agent at equal tokens (searched, limited tools).
agent_test: This is the key open experiment: arms = no check, re-solve k old problems per lesson (k=1,3,5,10), re-solve random vs most-similar old problems; metric = hold rate on old set plus gain on new lesson.

claim: Prioritised or interference-based replay gives small, inconsistent gains over uniform replay: MIR +2.8% accuracy and -2.5% forgetting on MNIST Split, PER wins 41 of 49 Atari games (RL), but an independent benchmark finds no clear winner among replay variants and tuned ER is very strong.
agent_test: Compare random vs most-conflicting regression picks per lesson. Expect a small effect; build only if it beats random at equal tokens.

claim: Offline compute over a store pays on predictable queries and at low test-time budgets, but not always: 5x on rebuilt benchmarks falls to about 1.5x on SWE-Features and reverses at high budget.
agent_test: Run an idle-time pass that derives implied inferences (reversals, derived rules) from the lesson store; count its tokens against later savings. Lampinen 2025 supports the idea in weights (fine-tune on in-context inferences).
